Approved on the merits — see my review above. Heads up: I just merged your #1351
into `main`, and since both PRs restructure the same tail end of
`stopsForLocationHandler`, this branch has picked up merge conflicts.

Please merge `main` in and resolve. The two changes are complementary — #1351
wrapped the reference block in the `includeReferences` guard, and this one
replaces the time parsing further up — so the resolution should be mechanical.
Once it's mergeable it's good to go; no re-review needed unless the resolution
changes behavior.

FYI (non-blocking, no code change needed): did a full spec-conformance pass on this while reviewing and updated the wiki with what we found — no action needed here.

- Documented the malformed-`time` fallback (falls back to current time rather than erroring), which matched legacy but wasn't written down: [stops-for-location § Extensions, 4a](https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/wiki/stops-for-location#extensions).
- Traced legacy's actual timezone handling for the current-time fallback: Java resolves it from the server JVM's own default timezone (a single process-wide setting), never per-agency. Your fix — resolving it against the queried agency's timezone instead — is a deliberate improvement over that, not a literal port of Java's mechanism, so it's now written up as its own decision rather than left implied: [stops-for-location § Implementation Decisions](https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/wiki/stops-for-location#implementation-decisions).
- Flagged the `agencies[0]` stand-in this (and `trips-for-location`) uses for "the queried agency" as a single-feed-limitation deviation, tracked in the [Multi-Agency-Static-Feeds-Stop-Consolidation §10 table](https://github.com/OneBusAway/maglev/wiki/Multi-Agency-Static-Feeds-Stop-Consolidation#10-deviations-from-legacy-due-to-the-single-feed-limitation) to revisit once multi-feed support lands.

Nice catch on the pre-existing UTC-fallback bug, and thanks for the reproduction detail in your commit message — made this easy to verify.

Nice catch on the underlying bug — `fmt.Sscanf(timeStr, "%d", &timeMs)` happily
reading `2025` off the front of `2025-06-13_14-00-00` and resolving to 1970 is
exactly the kind of silent wrong-answer that's hard to notice from the outside.

Things I checked and that hold up:

- It routes through `utils.ParseTimeParameter` rather than growing another
  parser, which is what CONTRIBUTING.md's Code Reuse section asks for and what
  trips-for-route, stops-for-route, vehicles-for-agency and trips-for-location
  already do. Epoch-vs-string disambiguation is handled inside that helper, so
  a digit-only string can't be mis-read as a date.
- Dropping the 15-minute binning is safe — `queryTime` fed exactly one consumer,
  `.Format("20060102")`, so binning to a quarter hour never affected anything.
- The second commit is the one I'd have asked for if it weren't here: a service
  date is a local calendar date, so taking the fallback in the agency's zone
  rather than the server clock's is correct, and it brings this in line with
  trips-for-location.
- `TestStopsForLocationUsesAgencyDateForCurrentTime` is the good test — two
  instants that are the same local Friday but straddle UTC midnight will fail
  if the fallback ever drifts back to the server zone. That's a real regression
  guard, not a shape check.
- Serving a malformed `time` as 200 rather than 400 preserves legacy behavior,
  and thanks for calling that out in the description rather than leaving me to
  spot it — that's the discrepancy handling CONTRIBUTING.md asks for.

Non-blocking: the comment at the `currentDate` line still reads "for the
requested queryTime", but `queryTime` is the variable this PR deleted. Worth a
one-word fix next time you're in the file.

Merging.
